article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid , generally indica-leaning
Genetics: Wedding Cake × 2 Scoops
Breeder: Elev8 Seeds
THC Content: Very high
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , Limonene , Myrcene
Primary Flavors: Orange sherbet, grape, creamy citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Medium
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Few cannabis names capture the intended flavor as neatly as Sherbet Cake . Its genetic design puts orange creamsicle, grape fruitiness, pastry sweetness, and Kush-influenced gas into the same flower, but the result is not merely sugary. Beneath the brighter sherbet character sits pepper, earth, dough, and a heavier fuel note inherited from Wedding Cake.

Elev8 developed the cultivar around a prized California 2 Scoops cut whose aroma reminded the breeder of old-school orange push pops, then crossed it with Wedding Cake specifically to deepen the profile with Cookies-style gas. The combination creates weed that can smell playful and confectionery while delivering a considerably more substantial hybrid experience than its dessert name might imply.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct pedigree is Wedding Cake × 2 Scoops. Elev8 identifies 2 Scoops as a T-Fly Genetics creation made by combining Grape Sherbet and Orange Sherbet , a pairing valued for colorful flowers, strong resin production, creamy citrus, grape, berries, and an unusually loud sherbet aroma. 2 Scoops is a balanced hybrid with sweet orange, creamy citrus, fruity berries, earth, and funk. Rather than covering those characteristics with an unrelated parent, Elev8 chose Wedding Cake to add density, potency, dough, spice, and gas.

Wedding Cake contributes a very different flavor architecture. The cultivar traces to Triangle Kush × Animal Mints and commonly expresses vanilla, pepper, butter-like richness, citrus, and earthy Kush tones. Caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene frequently appear prominently in Wedding Cake laboratory profiles. Put together, the family tree explains why Sherbet Cake can shift from nostalgic orange-and-grape candy into creamy dough and petroleum-like funk.
Effects and Experience

The early portion of the experience often fits the brighter side of its ancestry. 2 Scoops is associated with talkative, creative , happy effects, giving some context for why Sherbet-dominant phenotypes may begin socially rather than immediately heavy. A moderate amount can produce a noticeable change in mood while making music, food, casual conversation, gaming, or an easy creative activity more absorbing. The cerebral component is generally better characterized as loose and pleasant than sharply productive; complex work and demanding concentration may become less appealing as THC levels rise.

Wedding Cake influence becomes increasingly relevant as the session develops. Physical tension can soften, the pace slows, and the initial brightness gradually gives way to a more grounded body sensation. Wedding Cake itself is strongly associated with relaxation and sedation, so phenotypes leaning toward that parent may become particularly comfortable later in the evening. Elev8 rates Sherbet Cake’s potency as “very high” without assigning a fixed THC percentage, making actual laboratory testing important. Consumers with limited tolerance should approach slowly because excessive THC can turn comfortable euphoria into dizziness, dry mouth, anxious thinking, or pronounced lethargy.
Medical Benefits

For medical marijuana consumers, the cultivar’s potential usefulness comes from its combination of mood alteration and physical relaxation rather than from any proven strain-specific treatment effect. Someone dealing with stress may appreciate the mentally lighter beginning, while the more settled second half can make muscle tension or everyday discomfort feel less prominent. Heavier consumption may also encourage rest, though Sherbet Cake should not automatically be considered a dedicated sleep strain because individual phenotypes and doses can preserve substantial cerebral activity.

There are no clinical trials showing that Sherbet Cake specifically treats pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another medical disorder. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes that cannabis and cannabinoids may provide benefits for some chronic-pain conditions, while evidence concerning anxiety is limited and depends on the cannabinoid preparation studied. High-THC marijuana can also produce unwanted psychological effects, so medical consumers should consider their own tolerance, medications, laboratory testing, and professional medical advice rather than relying on a strain name alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sherbet Cake’s aromatic identity begins with 2 Scoops. Elev8 describes that parent as unusually loud, frosty, and strongly reminiscent of old-fashioned orange push pops. Those characteristics can produce an opening aroma of orange sherbet, grape candy, citrus cream, and ripe berries. Breaking the flower apart tends to reveal the darker Wedding Cake influence: cookie dough, pepper, earthy Kush, vanilla, and gas begin pushing through the fruit.

Its likely terpene balance reflects those intersecting families rather than one guaranteed chemical recipe. Caryophyllene commonly leads Wedding Cake profiles and has also been reported as dominant in cultivated 2 Scoops products; limonene and myrcene frequently appear around the Wedding Cake side. On the inhale, sweet orange cream and grape may arrive first, followed by vanilla cake or sugary dough. The exhale becomes drier and more adult, carrying pepper, earth, herbs, and fuel. That transition keeps the cultivar from becoming a one-dimensional candy strain and gives carefully cured flower considerably more depth.
Growing Information

Elev8’s own cultivation information is concise but useful: Sherbet Cake is a feminized photoperiod hybrid, finishes in approximately eight to nine weeks, and carries a medium yield rating. The breeder selected 2 Scoops partly for its exceptional frost, then introduced Wedding Cake for additional potency and terpene complexity. Growers should therefore expect resin production to become a major feature as flowering advances. Depending on phenotype, plants may show either a more colorful Sherbet expression or a denser, greener Cake structure.

Topping and low-stress training are practical ways to distribute growth across several flowering sites rather than allowing one central cola to dominate. Once dense buds begin forming, selective interior pruning improves airflow and helps strong light reach productive branches. Humidity control becomes increasingly important during late bloom because compact cannabis flowers can retain moisture around interior calyxes. Elev8 does not publish an official outdoor harvest date, but an eight-to-nine-week flowering window generally places mature outdoor plants around late September into early October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates; this is an estimate rather than breeder-specified timing. Trichome development, calyx swelling, and overall plant maturity remain better harvest indicators than the calendar alone.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Sherbet Cake?
Elev8 Seeds bred Sherbet Cake from Wedding Cake × 2 Scoops. The 2 Scoops parent was created by T-Fly Genetics from Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet.
Who bred Sherbet Cake?
The version covered here was bred by Elev8 Seeds. Elev8 has since retired the original seed release, but its breeder page remains available and preserves the genetic and flowering information.
Is Sherbet Cake indica or sativa?
Elev8 labels the cultivar simply as a hybrid. Its effects can nevertheless begin fairly bright and social before stronger physical relaxation develops.
What does Sherbet Cake taste like?

The profile combines orange sherbet, grape, creamy citrus, berries, sweet cake dough, vanilla, earth, spice, and cookie-like gas. The fruity side comes primarily from 2 Scoops, while Wedding Cake deepens the profile with richer dough and Kush characteristics.
How long does Sherbet Cake take to flower?
Elev8 specifies an indoor flowering period of approximately eight to nine weeks. The breeder rates production as medium rather than presenting an exaggerated fixed yield figure.
Final Thoughts on Sherbet Cake

Sherbet Cake succeeds because its parents contribute clearly different pieces of the finished profile. T-Fly Genetics’ 2 Scoops brings orange push-pop nostalgia, grape fruitiness, creamy citrus, colorful flower, and frost, while Wedding Cake adds dough, pepper, resin, potency, and the heavier gas needed to keep the sweetness grounded. Elev8’s decision to combine them produced a cannabis hybrid with a flavor identity that is easy to recognize without feeling simplistic.

For consumers, the attraction lies in that movement from fruit and cream toward earthier Cake richness, accompanied by effects that can progress from sociable euphoria into deeper relaxation. Growers get an eight-to-nine-week flowering cultivar with medium yield and strong resin potential rather than a plant bred solely for bulk production. Although Elev8 has retired the original seed release, Sherbet Cake remains an interesting example of modern dessert breeding done with contrast in mind: bright sherbet terpenes on one side, dense Cookies-and-Kush character on the other.
